name: Bengaluru
tagline: Eternal-Spring Climate and Cosmopolitan Comforts in India's Tech Capital
description: Bengaluru is India's tech capital, a sprawling garden city where multinational offices, craft breweries, and leafy parks sit side by side. Its roughly 920-meter elevation delivers the mildest year-round climate of any major Indian metro, trading Delhi's extreme heat and Chennai's humidity for warm days and genuinely cool evenings. A large, well-established tech and returnee community keeps English widely spoken and international comforts — specialty coffee, imported groceries, global cuisine — easy to find. Legendary traffic congestion is the city's defining frustration, but for FIRE seekers chasing comfort and cosmopolitan amenities at Indian prices, Bengaluru is hard to beat.

quickFacts.visa: India has no retirement, pension, or passive-income visa. US citizens use the e-Tourist visa — 30-day (double-entry) or 1-year/5-year (multiple-entry; the 5-year fee rose from $80 to $200 in 2026) — and may stay up to 180 days per visit, with total time capped at 180 days per calendar year; long-term residents get by cycling visas in and out. The only path to living in India indefinitely is the OCI card, open to people of Indian origin or those married 2+ years to an Indian citizen or OCI holder.
quickFacts.internetSpeed: 75–150 Mbps typical; excellent fiber up to 1 Gbps
quickFacts.safetyRating: Generally safer than Delhi or Mumbai with low violent crime; heavy traffic is the real day-to-day danger
quickFacts.climate: Mild for the tropics thanks to ~920 m elevation — warm days, cool evenings, June–October monsoon

1M.lifestyle: A comfortable 2-bedroom apartment in Jayanagar or HSR Layout, getting around on the expanding Namma Metro plus autos and ride-hailing apps. Eating at Bengaluru's beloved darshinis and casual restaurants most days, with regular visits to the city's famous craft-beer scene. Private health insurance covers Manipal and Fortis hospitals. The mild, near-constant spring-like climate keeps A/C costs low — a real advantage over Delhi or Chennai — even as traffic remains the city's biggest daily annoyance.
